comparison.objective: Safely zero a slicer gauge, release its carriage, and place the carriage on a cleaning tray; candidate commissions and locks a shock absorber through repeated impact trials.
comparison.physical_skill: Some shared knob rotation/regrasping, but slicer tests safety sequencing, multi-turn release, and bimanual carriage removal/carrying; candidate tests recessed hex-key engagement, collar counterholding, bounded locking torque, and response-based tuning.
comparison.success_condition: Slicer requires gauge ≤0.5 mm before carriage motion, release ≥1,060°, safe blade-zone avoidance, and flat tray placement. Candidate requires two repeatable ≥0.85 J cycles within stroke/rebound/overload limits plus post-lock drift resistance.
comparison.reason: The shared rotary primitive does not test the same ability. Slicer fidelity omits real threads/gearing and uses a switched interlock; candidate instead depends on physical lock retention and dynamic damping behavior. Candidate still lacks a numeric collar-drift tolerance and manufacturer values for setscrew torque, friction, and damping-versus-setting.
